children: Posco Holdings' steel business could report weaker 4Q earnings due to maintenance work, Daiwa Capital's Mike Oh and Daeho Son write in a note. The analysts say the Korean company's steel spreads could narrow in October-December because raw-material prices could rise further. On a 3Q earnings call earlier this week, management said the planned shutdown of a blast furnace in Gwangyang would reduce steel sales by 570,000 metric tons in 4Q 2026 and 430,000 metric tons in 1Q 2027. Daiwa notes that Posco raised its capacity utilization to 90.9% in 3Q ahead of the maintenance work, boosting production enough to offset higher raw-material costs. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
